page.layout: One column of running text, with a marginal mark at the right edge beside the middle lines. Running head at the top, page number at top right, gathering signature and catchword at the foot.

main_text.p: controuersia constat, cū (ut Cornificius ait) alia lex iubet, aut permittit, alia uetat quidpiam fieri: uel, ut Cicero scribit, cum inter se duæ uidētur leges, aut plures discrepare, hoc modo: Lex, Qui tyrannum occiderit, quam uolet sibi rem à magistratu deposcito, & magistratus ei cõcedito. Et altera lex, Tyrãno occiso quinq; eius proximos cognatione magistratus ne-canto. Tyrannū uxor sua no[?]stu, cum simul cubaret, occi-dit. Hæc filium suum, quem ex tyranno habebat, sibi præmij loco deposcit. Sunt qui ex lege puerum dicant occidi o-

page.notes: The text is printed in a single column; the running head reads "IVRIS CONSVLTI" with the spacing as printed, and the page number 181 is set in the head. Doubtful: the running head letters, and "no[?]stu" where the printed hyphen at the line end is unclear. The sign at the right margin beside the lines "canto" and "fua no" looks like a handwritten pointing mark or ink scribble rather than printed type, so it is not transcribed. The first word of the page, "controuersia", is a continuation from the previous page. The catchword "por" and the signature "m. 3" are printed at the foot.
